mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 6 months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >1% per month for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during INDPRO contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 2% combined with a concurrent rise in the Consumer Price Index above 4% suggests a monetary policy lag and inflation surprise, which typically precedes a positive equity market reaction as rate cuts are anticipated, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% AND CPIAUCSL > 104 (i.e., >4%) in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods of rapid payroll growth.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 3% year-over-year signals a broad-based demand shock, which depresses corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, especially in non-recessionary regimes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such demand shock episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for six consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which raises earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained INDPRO expansion.
